events.text: A young swordsman with too much hair and too little patience blocks your road. 'They say you were someone once. Prove it.'

ok.log: One move. He sits in the dust, staring at his empty hands. Then he bows, properly, for the first time in his life.

fail.log: Your knees are not what they were. He wins, and does not look as happy as he expected.

effects.log: By the third bowl of noodles he is telling you about his father. By the fifth you are giving advice. He leaves a different man, a little.

events.text: Your hands shake too much for the sword some mornings, but not for the brush. Someone suggests you write it all down.

effects.log: You leave nothing out: the fear, the luck, the mistakes. Young people copy it by hand and pass it around.
Every fight is a little longer in the telling, every enemy a little taller. It sells very well.

choices.text: Burn the first page and go fishing

effects.log: Some things are better left in the river. The fish are biting.

events.text: A letter arrives in handwriting you have not seen in forty years: an old friend from your youth, writing from their deathbed.

effects.log: You arrive in time. You sit together and say very little. It is enough. It is exactly enough.
You write all night. You never find out whether the letter arrived in time.

events.text: You lose another tooth biting a walnut, the way you have cracked walnuts all your life.

effects.log: You laugh so hard at yourself that the whole teahouse joins in. Old age is a long joke with a known ending.

events.text: Village children are playing 'murim heroes' in the square. One of them is pretending to be you. Badly.

effects.log: You spend the afternoon teaching children how to hold a stick. It is the best afternoon of the year.
You did not know anyone told stories about you. You go home quietly pleased.

events.text: You pass the grave of someone who once tried very hard to kill you. The weeds are high. Nobody else visits.

effects.log: You pull weeds for an hour and talk to the stone about the old days. You find you are not angry any more.
You do not stop. Some things stay unfinished, and that is also an ending.

events.text: Lying awake, you realise everything you know will be buried with you unless you give it to someone.

effects.log: You write every form you know into a plain notebook and leave it where someone worthy will find it.
The river does not keep the shape of the boat. You sleep well that night.

events.text: A cough settles into your chest this winter and does not want to leave.

choices.text: Breathe it out with your internal energy

ok.log: By spring it is gone. The old methods still work, even in an old body.

fail.log: It lingers until the plum trees bloom. You feel every one of your years.

effects.log: Bitter medicine and three weeks in bed. You grumble through all of it and recover.

events.text: You want to see the mountain where it all began one more time before your legs refuse the stairs.

effects.log: It takes you three days instead of one morning. At the top the wind is exactly as it was. You were not, and that is fine.

choices.text: Look at it from the valley

effects.log: It is smaller from here. So are the things that once seemed so important.

events.text: An old stranger in the teahouse keeps beating you at go, which has not happened in thirty years.

ok.log: You win the last game by half a point. He laughs, pays for the tea, and you never see him again.

fail.log: He wins again. You spend the week studying the board and understand something new about patience.

effects.log: He only smiles and says he is nobody. Later you learn a Transcendent was seen in the town that week.
